deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 81 is a page of German prose lecture notes on ancient Greek history. It continues from the previous page, which covered the rebuilding and fortification of Athens and the Piraeus after the Persian Wars. Its content, in order:

(1) On the expedition of 470 (as dated in the notes) under Pausanias, the leadership of Greece passed to Athens. Pausanias' arrogance alienated the allies, who defected and gave Athens the supreme command.

(2) Pausanias negotiated secretly with the Persians, who promised to make him overlord of Greece. When this came out, he was stripped of his command and recalled to Sparta, where he was killed.

(3) Under Spartan leadership the alliance had been purely military. Under Athens, Aristides and Cimon reorganised it. Every member state now paid an annual contribution into a common treasury. The notes give this as 460 talents and gloss 1 talent as 1200 fl. (Gulden/florins). The treasury was first kept on Delos and administered by Aristides. This is the Delian League (phoros).

(4) This opened the way for Athens to enlarge its power and influence, and to conceive the idea of hegemony (Oberherrschaft) over Greece.

(5) The last line is uncertain. It continues onto the next page with '...Unterthanen geworden, denn jeder Staat behielt seine Verfassung'. That is, the allies had not actually become subjects, since each state kept its own constitution.

The only quantitative content is the tribute figure and the currency conversion. Implied by me: 460 talents × 1200 fl. = 552,000 fl. per year.

The style, a dated narrative with a conversion into Gulden, matches Göttingen-era lectures on ancient history, possibly in the tradition of A. H. L. Heeren. Whether the hand is Gauss's own or a student's or family member's notes kept among his papers is unsure. Nothing here bears on Lagrange or on mathematics.
errors: Grammatical slip: 'worauf er seines Kommandos entsetzt und nach Sparta gefordert' lacks the auxiliary 'wurde'.

Chronology (carried over from the previous page): the allied expedition under Pausanias to Cyprus and Byzantium is usually dated 478 BC, not 470. The transfer of hegemony and the founding of the Delian League are dated 478/477 BC.

The 460-talent figure agrees with Thucydides 1.96. The conversion '1 Talent = 1200 fl.' is a period approximation that varies by source. It is not an error as such, but it is not a standard fixed value.
Pausanias' death (starved in the temple of Athena Chalkioikos) is usually placed later, c. 470s/460s BC. The compressed narrative is acceptable for lecture notes.

results.what: Narrative of the transfer of Greek hegemony from Sparta to Athens and the founding of the Delian League (460-talent annual tribute, treasury on Delos administered by Aristides).
results.modern_name: Delian League / Athenian hegemony (ancient Greek history)
results.usually_credited_to: Thucydides (Book 1.94–97); standard 18th–19th c. textbook and lecture material (e.g. Heeren)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine historical lecture notes on 5th-century BC Greece, with no mathematical content. It may not even be in Gauss's hand. Nothing here is mathematically or historically novel.

checkable.asserts: Annual tribute of 460 talents at 1200 fl. per talent equals 552,000 Gulden (implied conversion).

transcription_corrections: Line 'worauf er seines Kommandos entsetzt und nach Sparta gefordert': the image indeed lacks 'wurde', so this is the writer's omission, not a transcription error.
'(1 Talent 1200 fl.)' is confirmed in the image; the closing parenthesis is followed by 'und wurden im Anfang'.

The final line ('Die Spartaner aber / kaum[?] Unterzogen[?] als wären[?] sie darüber sehr ärgerlich[?]') is very uncertain. Given that the next page begins 'unterthanen geworden, denn jeder Staat behielt seine Verfassung', the sentence likely concerns the allies (Bundesgenossen/Verbündeten) not having become actual subjects ('... nicht ... Unterthanen geworden'). It probably does not concern Spartan annoyance. Re-read against the image.
The deleted 'A' before 'Oberkommando' and the deleted 'M' before 'militärisch' are correctly marked as strike-throughs. The struck 'betr' before 'betrugen' is also correctly marked.
